lines.text: Stop posting clips until you fix these three mistakes that pay you zero.
Here's the fix for each, step by step.
Quick refresher: a campaign pays you for the views your clip gets.
Right now the typical rate is around one dollar per thousand views.
But a rejected clip earns nothing, however many views it got.
Mistake number three: skipping the brief.
Every campaign lists what it wants: a tag, a handle, a length, a disclosure.
Miss one line, and the whole clip gets thrown out.
Mistake number two: using one clip twice.
A post can only go into one campaign, one time.
Same edit with a new logo still counts as reused.
Mistake number one, the big one: clipping the boring part.
People scrub a six hour stream, get tired, and cut anything.
The fix is letting the chat pick for you.
Clipzy reads the live chat and flags the second it spikes.
It cuts about thirty seconds around that spike, flips it vertical, and adds captions.
Keep the good ones, skip the rest, and check each against the brief.
It works on old replays too, so last week's streams count.
And three rules that never change.
Only clip creators and campaigns that allow it, and never pay to join one.
Never buy views either, because that's a permanent ban.
Fix these three today, before your next clip goes up.
Comment clip, and I'll message you the link.
